policy: Every Repair-adjacent capability surface across the governance root, the canonical product root, and the isolated specification repository carries exactly one RETAIN/ADAPT/RETIRE/BLOCK disposition with an accountable owner, a target phase, and a load-bearing negative test or evidence reference. A BLOCK requires enforcement. Phase 0 never enables a later-phase capability. Verified by scripts/trust-kernel/verify-repair-phase0-ledger.mjs (fail closed).

roots.note: Read-only evidence and pinned claim/certification linters. 105 pre-existing changes preserved; never edited or cleaned by Phase 0.
Canonical product main. Execution branch codex/repair-intelligence-phase0-trust transplants Trust Kernel commits 43301f96..8dfe0cc0 (24 commits, no dist).
Isolated non-authoritative specification repository. Holds the approved specification and the Phase 0 plan only.

surfaces.enforcement: Browser role is a display hint only; no actor role/name crosses the API. Server identity is derived from the verified user bearer and current database membership (S17-1, migration 0162).
surfaces.negativeTestId: supabase/functions/factory-api/index.test.ts: S17-1 spoof resistance and server-owned audit context

surfaces.enforcement: Verified bearer, current membership, one-time verified action context. Service role and anon key can never create or consume human authority.

site_code is a compatibility attribute, not the legal tenant boundary. Canonical authority is tenant -> organization -> site with current membership and site grant checks; no legal-scope substitution.

Organization becomes the normalized parent of site (migration 0189, Task 4); the verified action context pins organization_id via a transaction-time scope check. The caller never supplies authoritative organization identity.
Internal legacy pattern only; never Repair production evidence. Direct authenticated execution is revoked by migration 0190 (Task 6).
Broad authenticated storage policies (field_media_insert/field_media_select) are removed by migration 0190; no replacement evidence policy exists in Phase 0.
Reusable legacy signed URLs are never accepted as Repair evidence access; the legacy download route is blocked by default (REPAIR_PHASE_NOT_ENABLED).
GET/HEAD artifact byte routes return 423 REPAIR_PHASE_NOT_ENABLED before verification or CAS access; default server bootstrap never enables SHADOW_LEGACY.

The default handler rejects client-selected raw_uri with 423 REPAIR_PHASE_NOT_ENABLED before any OCR or provider egress; the legacy path is reachable only through explicit test/shadow dependency injection.
Provenance is retained; signer eligibility is redesigned in the approved Phase 1A plan. No Phase 0 human review queue exists.
Generic work-item/approval machinery carries no Repair work-order authority in Phase 0; WORK_ORDER is deny-only via the Repair Phase 0 capability contract.
No second ledger is created; PAYMENT and PROCUREMENT are deny-only in Phase 0 and any Phase 2 adoption requires reconciliation review.
Single mutable release authority and open-world egress sweep enforced by scripts/trust-kernel/verify-route-ledger.mjs (discovered == ledgered).
PWA-first; any Phase 3 adoption requires server-side idempotency. NATIVE_MOBILE is deny-only in Phase 0.
Integration only, never authoring. BIM_AUTHORING is deny-only in Phase 0.

R8-R12, professional sign-off, work order, procurement, payment, automated diagnosis, repair prescription, and execution authority are deny-only in Phase 0 via the Repair Phase 0 capability policy (REPAIR_PHASE_NOT_ENABLED).

The isolated repair-intelligence-app remains non-authoritative: it does not import product modules, write the canonical database, or become a second identity, artifact, AI, workflow, audit, or finance authority.
Claim and certification linters are pinned to governance commit 55557d7f178dcbe00fec15cffb3061df668eaff8 in CI; missing tools fail the job.
